newsitem.title: FINLAND: NEW FINNAIR PLANE LONG-TERM WORKHORSE - CEO.
newsitem.headline: NEW FINNAIR PLANE LONG-TERM WORKHORSE - CEO.

text.p: The new aircraft type Finnish national carrier Finnair will buy from either Airbus or Boeing will serve as the airline's workhorse long into the future, Finnair chief executive Antti Potila said on Friday.
"The project now at hand is particularly significant because the type of aircraft to be selected will be our company's "basic tool" long into the future," Potila said in a statement.
Finnair said it would invite offers from Airbus and Boeing for 12 new aircraft -- an acquisition expected to cost around two billion markka -- to replace its fleet of ageing DC9s.
"The company also plans to eventually replace the present MD80s with the aircraft chosen," Finnair said.
Its 12 DC9 planes to be gradually retired are on average 19 years old and the average age of its current fleet of 25 MD80 planes is slightly over eight years.
"The contract is to include options for eventual acquisition of additional aircraft on the same terms," Finnair said.
